disclaimer.title: Before you begin
disclaimer.intro: Nodekeeper helps you run your own Bitcoin node and manage ordinals. A few things to understand first:
disclaimer.selfCustody: This is self-custody. You alone hold your keys and your recovery phrase.
disclaimer.noRecovery: Nobody — including Nodekeeper — can recover your funds if you lose your recovery phrase. There is no "forgot password" option.
disclaimer.practiceFirst: Practice on Regtest first. It uses test coins with no real value, so you can try everything safely before using mainnet.
disclaimer.mainnetIsReal: Mainnet uses real bitcoin. Every mainnet transaction is real and, once broadcast, cannot be undone.

binarySetup.title: Set up Bitcoin Core and ord
binarySetup.intro: Nodekeeper downloads these directly from their official sources and verifies them before use -- Bitcoin Core against its maintainers' checksums and signatures, ord against a hash Nodekeeper has pinned in advance. Nothing runs until it passes.

indexOptions.title: Choose what ord indexes
indexOptions.intro: Each option unlocks more of ord's features, but turning one on later means a full reindex from scratch -- so it's worth deciding now. Regtest defaults to everything since it costs almost nothing there; a mainnet node with every option needs well over 1 TB of SSD space.
indexOptions.satsHint: Sat-level views, including every inscription on a sat when reinscribing.
indexOptions.permanenceNote: These choices are effectively permanent once ord has indexed -- changing them later means a full reindex from scratch.
indexOptions.tryItSafelyHint: Saves these choices, then opens the Regtest Test Lab -- practice with test coins before starting a multi-day mainnet sync.

testLab.title: Test Lab
testLab.intro: Safe practice mode on Regtest -- test coins have no real value, and you mine blocks yourself instead of waiting for real miners.
testLab.wrongEnvironment: The Test Lab only works on Regtest. Switch environment to use it.
testLab.oneClickSetupHint: Starts Bitcoin Core and ord, then mines 101 blocks to your wallet so its coins are spendable right away.
testLab.needsWalletFirst: Create a wallet on the Wallet screen first.
testLab.resetHint: Stops Regtest's services and deletes only its data -- other environments are never touched.
testLab.resetConfirmDescription: This stops Regtest and permanently deletes its wallet and blockchain data. Test coins have no real value, but this can't be undone.

list.title: Guided walkthroughs
list.intro: Step-by-step practice runs, with the Live Command Monitor opened automatically so you can see exactly what's happening underneath.
list.anotherActive: Finish or exit the walkthrough in progress first.

a.title: Your first wallet and balance
a.description: Create a Regtest wallet, get a receive address, mine blocks to it, and watch your balance appear.

0.instructions: Click "Create wallet" here on the Wallet screen. It's free, instant, and only ever holds worthless test coins.

1.instructions: Find the "Receive address" shown on this screen -- that's where your test coins will go.

2.instructions: Back on the Test Lab, mine some blocks to your new wallet -- try "Get test coins", or mine 101+ for a spendable balance right away.

3.instructions: Back on the Wallet screen, your balance should now show a nonzero amount. That's it -- you just funded a Bitcoin wallet.

b.title: Inscribe your first file
b.description: Inscribe a file, mine a block to confirm it, then see it appear in your wallet's gallery.

0.instructions: Go to Inscribe, drop in a file, preview it, and inscribe it. (No node or ord running yet? Use the Test Lab's "One-click setup" first.)

1.instructions: Mine a block on the Test Lab to confirm it -- inscriptions don't show up anywhere until they're in a block.

2.instructions: Head to the Wallet screen -- your new inscription should now appear in the gallery below your balance.

c.title: Reinscribe onto an existing sat
c.description: Reinscribe an inscription you already own, mine a block, then see both inscriptions live together on the same sat.

0.instructions: Go to Inscribe > Reinscribe, pick {{targetInscriptionId}}, and create a new inscription on top of it.

1.instructions: Mine a block on the Test Lab to confirm the reinscription.

2.instructions: Look up sat {{targetSat}} in the Explorer -- you should see both inscriptions listed on it, in order.

e.title: Run a command and a script
e.description: Run a raw command in the Console and one of the example scripts, both visible live in the Command Monitor.

0.instructions: Go to Console and run any command -- try "getblockchaininfo" or "ord wallet balance".

1.instructions: Go to Scripts and run one of the example scripts against Regtest.
